title: Trace what each formulation does when an input disappears
description: Remove sensor evidence, then choose the direct model's missing-value policy. Compare an explicit fixed-input decision with a generative posterior that uses only the likelihood terms that arrived.
notice: This lab uses an illustrative logistic score and Gaussian Naive Bayes distributions. Real systems must validate calibration, independence assumptions, missingness patterns, and the safety of every fallback.

evidenceChoices.label: Both sensors arrived
evidenceChoices.detail: Temperature and vibration are available to both scoring paths.

evidenceChoices.label: Vibration is missing
evidenceChoices.detail: Score from temperature while deciding what the fixed-input model receives for vibration.

evidenceChoices.label: Temperature is missing
evidenceChoices.detail: Score from vibration while deciding what the fixed-input model receives for temperature.

evidenceChoices.label: No current sensors arrived
evidenceChoices.detail: The generative posterior falls back to the class prior; the direct path follows its explicit policy.

missingPolicies.label: Reject incomplete input
missingPolicies.detail: Return no direct prediction and route to a fallback or delayed retry.

missingPolicies.label: Fill population mean
missingPolicies.detail: Use a versioned training-population value for every missing feature.

missingPolicies.label: Use last known value
missingPolicies.detail: Carry forward the machine's previous measurement and accept staleness risk.

cases.label: Steady machine
cases.detail: Both measurements resemble the healthy class distribution.

cases.label: Likely bearing fault
cases.detail: Heat and vibration are both elevated relative to the healthy fleet.

cases.label: Conflicting sensors
cases.detail: Temperature is elevated while vibration still looks comparatively normal.
